Yes, cardiovascular evaluation is necessary prior to and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas. Beta-blockers, such as propranolol, are commonly used to treat infantile hemangiomas, but they can have potential cardiovascular side effects, including hypotension, bradycardia, and changes in cardiac output. 

A baseline cardiovascular evaluation is recommended before starting beta-blocker therapy to assess for any pre-existing cardiovascular conditions. This evaluation may include a physical examination, electrocardiogram (ECG), and echocardiogram. 

During beta-blocker therapy, regular monitoring of heart rate, blood pressure, and other cardiovascular parameters is also necessary to promptly identify and manage any potential side effects. This monitoring can help minimize the risks associated with beta-blocker therapy and ensure the safe and effective treatment of infantile hemangiomas.
